content.title: About
content.content: Kiwi is the edible fruit of the Actinidia deliciosa vine, native to China but now cultivated in subtropical and temperate regions worldwide. The fruit is oval, covered with a thin fuzzy skin that can be green or yellow, and inside it has bright green flesh dotted with tiny black seeds. Kiwi offers a refreshing sweet‑tart flavor and a fragrant aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kiwi is sometimes called the “Chinese gooseberry,” though its taste is closer to a berry.
In China it is known as the “hairy fruit,” while in New Zealand it is often referred to as the “golden berry.”
The “golden kiwi” variety has yellow flesh and a sweeter taste than the green type.
Kiwi contains about three times more vitamin C than an orange – roughly 90 mg per 100 g.
Kiwi seeds are a good source of omega‑3 fatty acids.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: Provides vitamin K and folate
items.content: These nutrients are important for blood clotting and healthy cell development.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Kiwi provides lutein and zeaxanthin, which are beneficial for eye health.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to kiwi, ranging from mild oral itching to swelling of the lips and throat.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The fruit’s acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Kiwi’s high vitamin K content may affect the efficacy of certain anticoagulant drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Kiwi can be eaten fresh by cutting it in half and scooping out the flesh with a spoon, added to salads, smoothies, yogurts, desserts, and baked goods. The skin is edible after a thorough wash, though most people prefer to peel it.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store kiwi at room temperature until they ripen (about 3–5 days). Once ripe, keep them in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, where they stay fresh for up to a week.
